title: Japan — Northern Alps in autumn
notes: Fifteen nights through the Northern Alps, sequenced north to south and high to low so it follows the autumn colour down the mountain rather than fighting it. The dates are a deliberate trade: Hakuba's alpine colour peaks late September, the Nakasendo's peaks late October, and those five weeks cannot both be caught in one trip — so this window takes the Kiso valley and Kamikochi's golden larch at their best and accepts Hakuba past its peak, where the colour has descended to the mid-mountain and the village. It also sits clear of the Sports Day holiday weekend entirely. Nothing is booked yet.

summary.note: Budget figures are the whole trip for two travellers, in MYR, and are planning estimates rather than quotes — nothing is booked. They exclude flights. The exchange rate is the mid-market rate on 14 Aug 2026 (1 MYR = 38.9 JPY), a placeholder until money is actually changed; every converted figure on the site moves with it. Day costs carry only fares that have been looked up and checked, as a group total for two, so the daily totals are well below what a day will really cost — the planning envelope is this table, not those.

overview.remarks: The larch turns golden roughly 25 Oct to 5 Nov — about a week behind the maples and the last spectacle of the season. The densest stands are right around the bus terminal and Konashidaira. Private cars are banned in the valley; bus or taxi only.

overview.remarks: The Torii Pass is the highest point on the Kiso Nakasendo, and Narai is the longest of the post towns and far quieter than Tsumago. Swap this for a slow day in Tsumago if the legs have had enough.

accommodation.remarks: Airport hotel — the flight lands at 22:15, so anything further in wastes a night.
Four nights on one base. The fourth is deliberate slack: Happo Pond needs a calm morning and this gives three chances at it. Ask about laundry.
Near the castle or the station both work; Nakamachi is the nicer evening walk.
Shin-Hotaka or Fukuji. A private or semi-open rotenburo is the whole point of these four nights.
Book this first. Fewer than ten properties inside the valley and late October sells out months ahead. Half board is the norm — there is nowhere else to eat after dark.
Edo-era minshuku in the post town itself. Late October is the busiest stretch of the year on the Nakasendo and the houses are small, so book early.

transport.mode: Trains, buses, gondolas and ropeways throughout — no hire car. Private vehicles are banned in Kamikochi, and nothing else on the route needs one.

todo.remarks: Do this first. Fewer than ten properties in the valley and the larch week sells out months ahead.
Second priority. Late October is the busiest stretch of the year on the Nakasendo and the houses have few rooms each. Book direct or through the Tsumago tourist office.
Shin-Hotaka or Fukuji. Four nights — worth paying for a private rotenburo on at least one.
Landing at 22:15 — pick something inside or shuttle-linked to the terminal.
Waiting on an ANA promotion. The Oct 2027 schedule should load around Nov 2026; confirm the times still match before committing the rest.
